newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy M2 at levels consistent with rate cut - BOI.
newsitem.headline: Italy M2 at levels consistent with rate cut - BOI.

text.p: The current growth of Italian money supply as measured by M2 is consistent with a reduction in interest rates, but monetary policy is still aimed at reducing inflation, the Bank of Italy said in its half yealy bulletin.
"The expansion of M2 is compatible with a reduction of interest rates, which will be all the greater the faster inflationary pressures fall," the report said.
"Monetary policy will continue to pursue with determination the objective of a durable reduction in inflation," it added.
According to latest data, M2 year-on-year in the three months to end-August was 4.4 percent. The Bank of Italy said in its bulletin on Friday that M2 should grow by less than five percent in 1997.
The Bank of Italy cut its official discount rate to 7.5 percent last week from a previous 8.25 percent and cut the fixed term advances rate by the same amount. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
